archetype.name: Fringe Contender (Lamar-dependent)
archetype.definition: A new-staff Ravens team with a top-ten offense when Lamar Jackson plays and a middling, deep-leaking defense, good enough to win the AFC North scrum but not good enough to survive long without its quarterback.

report.headline: A top-ten offense with Lamar, a stalled one without him; 4-3 is honest.
report.take:
Jesse Minter's first Ravens team is built around Lamar Jackson's passing and Derrick Henry's workload. Henry has 147 carries and nobody else has more than 21. With Jackson under center the offense looked like the 2024 version. Its passing EPA per play of 0.182 ranks 8th, and in his four starts the pass game produced 10.3, 3.3, 11.9 and 12.0 EPA. The defense is the same middle-of-the-pack unit as last year: 20th in EPA allowed this season, 18th in 2025. It is stingy underneath and soft over the top.

The season splits at Week 5, when Tyler Huntley replaced the injured Jackson. The first Huntley game, a 30-23 win at Atlanta, rode 208 rushing yards. Then the run game fell apart. Rushing EPA was -10.0 at Cleveland and -9.4 against Cincinnati, the offense scored 10 and 13 points, and Huntley took 3 and 4 sacks behind a line that ranks 10th in pressure rate allowed. Season-long marks like an 11th-ranked run EPA blend two different offenses. The Jackson version was efficient. The Huntley version could not stay on schedule once defenses stopped respecting the quarterback run.

The record is not lying. Wins over expected sits at -0.21, the point differential of +2 implies 4.2 wins, and the one-score record (0.6) is unremarkable. The bigger warning signs are self-inflicted. The Ravens rank 28th in penalties per game and 30th in line penalties, special teams rank 23rd, and the offense converts short yardage at a 30th-ranked 44.4%. A 131-penalty-yard afternoon turned an 11.5-point favorite against Tennessee into a 24-18 escape. These are fixable habits, not talent gaps, but a first-year staff has not fixed them yet.

Where this goes hinges on the ankle. Minter says Jackson is "in a decent spot" for Buffalo. If he is back for good, the schedule through Week 14 is soft enough (LAC at 0-6, HOU and TB at 2-5) to bank wins. Then comes a finish of four straight division games against Pittsburgh twice, Cleveland and Cincinnati, and that is where the AFC North will be settled.

strengths.title: Jackson-led passing efficiency
strengths.body: With Jackson, Baltimore's dropbacks were among the league's most productive, and that drives the 8th-ranked offensive EPA. Huntley's starts were far flatter, so the season rate understates the healthy version. It lasts exactly as long as Jackson's ankle does.

strengths.title: Line wins early on runs
strengths.body: Backs average 2.75 yards before contact (7th) and 4.36 per carry (7th), and pressure allowed ranks 10th. The 24th-ranked sack rate looks more like Huntley holding the ball than a protection failure, since the pressure rate itself is good. Losing guard Olaivavega Ioane (89% of snaps, knee) would test that.

strengths.title: Tight underneath, QB-hitting defense
strengths.body: The defense ranks 6th on short passes and is among the stingiest against tight ends and backs. It hits the quarterback at the 6th-best rate even though raw pressure ranks 24th. That shape forces long, patient drives, which suits a team that also ranks 7th in time of possession.

concerns.title: Run game collapses without Jackson
concerns.body: Henry's lanes depend on the threat of the quarterback keeping the ball. Once that disappeared, Cleveland and Cincinnati smothered the run and the offense scored 10 and 13. That is a structural QB dependency, not a slump, and it returns any time Jackson misses time.

concerns.title: No.1 receivers and deep balls
concerns.body: Opposing WR1s produce more EPA per target against Baltimore than against any other defense, and deep passes rank 26th. A light four-man rush gives quarterbacks time to push the ball downfield. With safety Jaylinn Hawkins out and LB Tavius Robinson on IR, the back end and the rush both get thinner.

concerns.title: Penalties, special teams, short yardage
concerns.body: Flags, a below-average kicking and return unit, and a 30th-ranked short-yardage rate leak hidden points every week. They are coachable, but seven games into a new regime they remain the profile. They have also helped push the Ravens to a 27th-ranked cover rate.

trend.note: The offense peaked with Jackson in Weeks 1-4, held up once in Atlanta behind the run, then sank to 10 and 13 points as the rushing EPA went deeply negative against Cleveland and Cincinnati.

nextGame.headline: A shootout at Buffalo, if Jackson's ankle lets Baltimore keep pace
nextGame.body:
Buffalo is the league's most lopsided team: 1st in offensive EPA and 1st in passing EPA, but 31st in EPA allowed and 29th against the pass. The Book has the Bills -3.5 with a 53.5 total, the shape of a game decided by who gets the last stop. Baltimore's best answer is its own healthy passing game plus ball control. The Ravens rank 7th in time of possession and the Bills 25th, and Buffalo's run defense ranks 22nd, so there is room for Henry. The danger on the other side is plain. Josh Allen's passing game meets a Ravens defense that is worst in the league against No.1 receivers and 26th on deep balls.

Availability swings it. Jackson is listed out with a return estimate of game day, and his coach sounds optimistic. His presence is the difference between the Weeks 1-4 offense and the one that just scored 13. Guard Olaivavega Ioane (knee) is questionable after leaving the Bengals game, and Baltimore loses safety Jaylinn Hawkins and LB Tavius Robinson on defense. Buffalo is without safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson to a suspension, which further thins an already leaky secondary, while WR DJ Moore and DT Ed Oliver are questionable.

waysToWin.title: Zay Flowers against a broken secondary
waysToWin.body: Buffalo lets opposing WR1s score further above their averages than any team in the league. Flowers leads Baltimore with 53 targets, and Gardner-Johnson's suspension removes a starting safety. A healthy Jackson throwing into that coverage is the most direct path to matching Buffalo score for score.

waysToWin.title: Henry drives keep Allen sidelined
waysToWin.body: Buffalo ranks 22nd against the run and 25th in time of possession. Long Henry-led drives shorten a game that the Bills' offense would otherwise win on volume. This only works if the Jackson threat is back to open the lanes.

waysToWin.title: Win the turnover battle
waysToWin.body: Baltimore has given the ball away just five times, while Buffalo sits 23rd in turnover margin. One extra possession in a game with a 53.5 total may be all it takes.

waysToLose.title: Allen picks apart the deep middle
waysToLose.body: The league's best passing offense meets a defense that is worst against No.1 receivers and 26th on deep throws, now without safety Hawkins. If Baltimore's light rush can't get home, Buffalo scores at will.

waysToLose.title: Jackson sits or is limited
waysToLose.body: If Huntley starts again, the offense that just managed -9.4 rushing EPA has to keep pace with the top scoring team. Buffalo's 6th-ranked pressure rate would also find a quarterback who took 4 sacks last week.

waysToLose.title: Hidden yardage tilts to Buffalo
waysToLose.body: Buffalo's special teams rank 4th and Baltimore's 23rd, and the Ravens' flags stall drives. Against an offense this good, giving up field position and free first downs is how a three-point game becomes a ten-point one.

nextGame.watch: Whether Jackson plays and is willing to run. That single factor decides if Henry's run game and the Flowers matchup exist at all.

restOfSeason.body:
With Jackson healthy, this is the offense that ranked near the top through four weeks, and the next stretch (JAX, winless LAC, CAR, HOU, TB) is forgiving enough to climb back above the AFC North pack. The record is not inflated, so there is no luck to give back. There is also no bad luck to recover. Improvement has to come from the quarterback returning and from cutting penalties and special-teams leaks.

The finish is the problem: four straight division games, with Pittsburgh and Cleveland bringing top-seven defenses and Cincinnati an offense that just hung 35 on Baltimore. The defense's deep-ball weakness and thin rush, now without Robinson, look sticky given last year's similar ranks. Expect a team that wins on offense and plays a lot of close games.
swingFactors: Jackson's ankle and how many more starts Huntley makes
Whether the pass defense can stop explosive WR1 production
The four-game division finish against PIT, CLE and CIN

confidence.note: Seven games split by a QB injury, a first-year staff, and Jackson's status unresolved.
